name: North Dakota
stateTaxAgencyName: North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner
dueDateNotes: North Dakota follows the federal schedule: April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15. If a due date falls on a weekend or holiday, it moves to the next business day.
selfEmploymentNotes: North Dakota starts from your federal taxable income (the federal standard deduction is already applied; there is no separate state deduction) and applies just three rates: 0%, 1.95%, and 2.5%. A large zero-rate bracket means the first $48,475 (single) or $80,975 (married) of taxable income is tax-free at the state level. Long-term capital gains get a 40% exclusion before these rates apply.
uniqueFacts: North Dakota has one of the lowest income tax structures in the country: just three rates topping out at 2.5%, with a large 0% bracket that exempts the first $48,475 (single) or $80,975 (married) of taxable income.
North Dakota excludes 40% of net long-term capital gains from taxable income.
North Dakota begins from your federal taxable income, so it has no separate state standard deduction.
